{{Short description|Topological space}}
In [[mathematics]], more specifically in [[topology]], the '''Volodin space''' <math>X</math> of a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] ''R'' is a subspace of the [[classifying space]] <math>BGL(R)</math> given by
:<math>X = \bigcup_{n, \sigma} B(U_n(R)^\sigma)</math>
where <math>U_n(R) \subset GL_n(R)</math> is the subgroup of upper [[triangular matrix|triangular matrices]] with 1's on the diagonal (i.e., the unipotent radical of the standard Borel) and <math>\sigma</math> a [[permutation matrix]] thought of as an element in [[general linear group|<math>GL_n(R)</math>]] and acting (superscript) by conjugation.<ref>{{harvnb|Weibel|2013|loc=Ch. IV. Example 1.3.2.}}</ref> The space is [[acyclic space|acyclic]] and the [[fundamental group]] <math>\pi_1 X</math> is the [[Steinberg group (K-theory)|Steinberg group]] <math>\operatorname{St}(R)</math> of ''R''. In fact, {{harvtxt|Suslin|1981}} showed that ''X'' yields a model for [[Plus construction|Quillen's plus-construction]] <math>BGL(R)/X \simeq BGL^+(R)</math> in [[algebraic K-theory]].

== Application ==

An analogue of Volodin's space where GL(''R'') is replaced by the [[Lie algebra]] <math>\mathfrak{gl}(R)</math> was used by {{harvtxt|Goodwillie|1986}} to prove that, after tensoring with '''Q''', relative ''K''-theory K(''A'', ''I''), for a nilpotent ideal ''I'', is isomorphic to relative [[cyclic homology]] HC(''A'', ''I''). This theorem was a pioneering result in the area of [[trace method]]s.
